item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. intelligence chief says Trump's description of Putin as a 'friend' is 'entirely appropriate'
item.description: Clayton defended comments that Democrats have characterized as a betrayal of American values after Trump met with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping for rare three-way talks.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats clinch a historic House majority of at least 258 seats, the largest since 1992
item.description: The 258-seat tally was reached Sunday after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Scientists are fighting for their halted funds. Trust of Black communities may be harder to win back
item.description: The study was among broader research into why Black Americans are twice as likely as their white peers to develop Alzheimer's, but the Trump administration abruptly halted it in its final stretch.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: French activists demand a tear gas suspension over reported menstrual changes
item.description: Some women reported painful cramps, unexpected bleeding and disrupted menstrual cycles after exposure, and an advocacy group says it has collected more than 10,000 complaints.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: As AI detects flaws in computer systems, is it causing more tech outages and disruptions?
item.description: AI rapidly identifies computer system vulnerabilities and companies are pressured to fix them. Experts say that might lead to unintended consequences, like tech outages.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mercury gets its first visitor in years as a pair of spacecraft loop into orbit
item.description: BepiColombo is only the third spacecraft to visit Mercury — the sun's closest planet and barely bigger than our moon — and the first in more than a decade.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: UN climate talks break down over bitter disagreements on fossil fuels
item.description: Expectations had already been low heading into the two-week negotiations in Turkey, but impasses over explicitly including fossil fuels and other issues, including money, proved irreconcilable.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Immigration officers make arrests at Seattle airport in 'distressing' scene, delaying flight
item.description: Video of the incident showed officers dragging away at least one person at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport as a woman screams that her daughter is being taken and she has a work permit.

item.title: NPR: Politics chat: Lawmakers step up with only weeks to Democrats' control of Congress
item.description: A funding deadline for Congress weeks before Democrats take control. President Trump signs an executive order requiring contractors to get approval before sharing with Congressional investigations.

item.title: NPR: Christian nationalist conference hosts Nick Fuentes, vows to keep pushing MAGA agenda
item.description: A particular group of Christian nationalists met in Texas last weekend and vowed to push what remains of MAGA as far to the right as possible. They hosted antisemitic streamer Nick Fuentes.

item.title: NPR: It's Medicare open enrollment time. Here's what you need to know
item.description: Open enrollment for Medicare runs through Dec. 7, and there are a few different pitfalls people should watch out for this year. Your drug plan or Medicare Advantage plan could be changing a lot.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Why do people believe recent tech failures must be connected?
item.description: Even without clear evidence, people drew connections between recent tech failures and outages. The way our brains and social media platforms work helps explain why.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: For families of the fallen, Trump's proposed arch casts a shadow over Arlington National Cemetery
item.description: Trump's proposed 250-foot-tall arch could cast a long shadow on Arlington National Cemetery, with the potential to literally shade gravesites, disrupt solemn visits with the noise of construction and alter the carefully designed historic landscape of the nation's capital.

item.title: NPR: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
item.description: President Trump is directing federal contractors to consult the White House about inquiries from Congress and to withhold any communications that his administration considers privileged.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump vows to work with Democrats to cap credit card interest rates at 10%
item.description: The standard proposal would substantially reduce what credit card companies can charge customers. The median credit card interest rate is roughly 22.2%, according to an August survey by the New York Federal Reserve.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: AP source: FBI investigating apparent hack of its key national criminal justice database
item.description: The National Crime Information Center, known as the NCIC, is a computerized database of criminal justice information that is available to local, state and federal law enforcement agencies and includes records on fugitives, missing persons, criminal history data, stolen property and other topics.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A doctor's guide to surviving — and enjoying — holiday feasting while on GLP‑1 medication
item.description: Changes in appetite, smaller portion tolerance, limits on alcohol consumption, medication side effects and the desire to maintain progress can make navigating holiday traditions feel a little different.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
item.description: The order is the Republican administration's latest effort to resist what are expected to be wide-ranging and aggressive oversight efforts from Democrats when they take over Congress in January.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mexico detains top cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro,' setting off a burst of violence in Sinaloa
item.description: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives. He climbed the cartel ranks to lead the Beltrán Leyva cartel and later became the leader of his own group, the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump auditions potential successors as Rubio and Vance join him for White House briefing
item.description: It was the latest episode in the public audition that the president and former reality television star has appeared to delight in arranging for his potential successors as he nears his last two years in office.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Climate talks in overtime as nations wrestle with response to worsening global warming
item.description: The added day of talks came as the two-week annual summit, or COP31, drew strong condemnation for failing to mention fossil fuels in a draft of the final agreement.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Texas says an execution went as planned. A witness says screams showed 'tremendous distress'
item.description: Executions across the U.S. have garnered more attention since Christa Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital in Tennessee in September. The drug didn't enter her bloodstream correctly.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Bessent says no further restrictions are needed for Nvidia chip exports to China
item.description: "The proper chip restrictions are in place," Bessent said in an interview with CNBC after returning from a trip to Asia with President Donald Trump. "And the remote access has been curtailed."

item.title: NPR: How a GOP redistricting 'dummymander' in North Carolina backfired by 2 seats
item.description: In North Carolina, Republican lawmakers redrew voting maps, aiming to gain one seat in Congress. Instead, they lost two seats, in a classic example of what political scientists call a "dummymander."

item.title: NPR: The New Yorker's Jason Zengerle on Hakeem Jeffries' rise to first Black House speaker
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries is set to become the first-ever African American speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Jason Zengerle of The New Yorker about the rise of Jeffries.

item.title: NPR: Week in Politics: Trump returns from Asia; hails trip as one of best in history
item.description: President Trump returned from his trip to Asia, saying it was one of the most successful presidential visits to that continent -- or anywhere else -- in American history.

item.title: NPR: An effort to circumvent the Electoral College may be within reach. But hurdles remain
item.description: A national effort to ensure that only winners of the popular vote become president could reach a critical milestone soon.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Rights groups urge sanctions after ICJ finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice has no power to enforce Thursday's ruling, which orders Myanmar's military-supported government to allow those who fled the violence to return home safely, to pay reparations to the Rohingya Muslims and prosecute those suspected of having committed genocide.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Federal jury convicts man of starting deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles
item.description: The man accused of sparking last year's deadly Palisades Fire was found guilty of arson charges Friday after his first federal case earlier this year ended in a mistrial.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What Trump addressed during his lengthy White House news conference
item.description: In a lengthy press conference, President Trump touted his recent trip to Asia and defended his relationship with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. White House correspondent Liz Landers was in the briefing room as the president took questions from reporters.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Stocks tumble as worries about AI rattle market
item.description: In our news wrap Friday, stocks tumbled to end the week as worries about AI rattled the market, a second federal judge is blocking President Trump's triumphal arch in Washington and a federal appeals court is blocking the Army from detonating several tons of bomb-making chemicals amid concerns over environmental and health risks.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mounting tech disruptions raise concerns about U.S. cybersecurity
item.description: President Trump has replaced the nation's top cybersecurity official following a string of seemingly unrelated technology outages over the last couple of weeks. Officials have repeatedly stressed that these outages were not the result of intentional attacks, but given the growth of AI, there's growing concern that attacks are on the horizon. William Brangham discussed more with Chris Krebs.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Josh Shapiro on foreign policy, Democratic wins and his 2028 ambitions
item.description: Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro is fresh off a reelection campaign that gave him another four years in office and Democrats majorities in the state House. Now Shapiro is turning his attention to foreign policy, laying out his prescriptions to solve pressing global crises. Amna Nawaz sat down with the governor to discuss his vision for how the United States should engage on the world stage.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Fiona's caretakers and fans mourn the beloved hippo after her death at Cincinnati Zoo
item.description: Born prematurely almost a decade ago and given slim odds of survival, Fiona became not only a source of hometown pride but also a worldwide symbol of hope and inspiration for many.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Brooks and Capehart on Trump's summit with Putin and Xi
item.description: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including President Trump's trilateral summit with Xi and Putin, the ongoing debate surrounding data centers, and Elon Musk's attempt to distance himself from MAGA.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Inside the museum preserving the story of JFK's assassination
item.description: On November 22, 1963, President John F. Kennedy was killed while driving in a motorcade in downtown Dallas. As the story continues to be told and questioned, those memories are preserved and displayed at The Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza. Senior arts correspondent Jeffrey Brown visited the museum for our arts and culture series, CANVAS.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Court approves $7.25 billion Bayer settlement over claims Roundup weed killer caused cancer
item.description: Agrochemical maker Bayer will pay up to $7.25 billion over two decades to resolve thousands of claims from U.S. cancer patients asserting the company should have warned people that its popular weed killer Roundup could cause lymphoma, according to a settlement approved Friday by a Missouri judge.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Activists, leaders criticize COP31 climate talks as fossil fuels go unmentioned in draft deal
item.description: United Nations climate talks in Turkey stretched into overtime Friday and delegates put off some decisions to next year, unable to find common ground on multiple issues with mutterings and protests about failure.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Lawsuits allege corner cutting, ignored warnings led to fatal Brooklyn building collapse
item.description: As investigators probe what caused a New York City building collapse that killed eight people, workers and residents are painting a portrait of two trouble spots side-by-side: the apartment house that fell down and the construction site being excavated next door.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: NATO calls Russian missiles landing in Poland a 'grave violation' of airspace
item.description: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday in what its prime minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine.

item.title: NPR: The latest from Trump's press conference
item.description: President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Second federal judge blocks construction of Trump's memorial arch
item.description: A second federal judge has blocked President Donald Trump's administration from building a 250-foot memorial arch in the nation's capital, issuing an order on Friday that keeps the construction work on hold indefinitely, according to plaintiffs' lawyers who sued to challenge the project.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Trump on data centers: 'Take advantage, don't shut them off'
item.description: The president said he doesn't want to allow the centers to be built outside the U.S. "because China will take all of them." He added that companies that try to build elsewhere will face "tremendous penalties."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Cascade of tech outages 'separate events' and 'under control,' Trump says
item.description: "If there's any silver lining to what happened last week, it's that Congress seems to be very receptive now to giving us the money," Trump said about the administration's plan to overhaul air traffic control.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Trump says he would love former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to 'be given a second chance'
item.description: "We have to protect our brilliant people. Jensen is one of them," Trump said during a press conference at the White House, touting Nvidia as "a very important company to us."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: 'We will not allow that to happen,' Trump says of reported Iran dirty bomb threat
item.description: "We know a lot about what's happening in Iran," Trump said, speaking during a press briefing at the White House. "We know everything they say. We know who they are, where they are. We'll find out about it."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Court grants request to prevent military from detonating bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
item.description: The detonation was initially planned for Friday, but the Army pushed it to Monday following an outpouring of public concern about the potential health and environmental consequences.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump defends calling Putin a friend, saying they have a 'very good' personal relationship
item.description: The Republican president appeared to sidestep a question about whether he sees Putin as a friend to the United States.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Northeastern Florida now under flood threats from heavy rain that has devastated coastal communities
item.description: Parts of Florida's east coast have been deluged with rainfall totaling more than 17 inches in some spots since Tuesday, according to preliminary totals by the weather service.

item.title: NPR: A second judge blocks Trump's arch, saying it's unlikely to succeed in court
item.description: A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against Trump's arch, going a step further than the D.C. federal judge who temporarily blocked construction earlier this week.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Travelers' concerns spike as Thanksgiving nears and tech hiccups grow, but few are dissuaded
item.description: Just like bad weather, air travel disruptions irritate many Americans while dissuading comparatively few.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mamdani sets plan to close NYC's notorious Rikers Island jail by 2032
item.description: The mayor unveiled the plan as the city is all but certain to blow past a legal requirement to close Rikers and replace it with four smaller, more modern jails by 2027.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Sales of 'Grand Theft Auto VI' hit more than $2.3 billion after long-anticipated release
item.description: The game, which launched on Thursday, has hit $2.36 billion in revenue with approximately 24.6 million units sold.

item.title: NPR: Trump initially accepted the midterm results, but most GOP voters doubt they were fair
item.description: Less than half of Republicans nationwide considered the midterm elections "free and fair," according to new polling.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Trump hosts news conference after meeting with Xi, Putin
item.description: Trump's meeting on Thursday was the first-ever sit-down for the leaders of the U.S., Russia and China.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Myanmar is the first state found responsible for genocide. Here's how the ICJ ruled in other cases
item.description: The International Court of Justice has been asked to reach that conclusion before, but never found enough evidence to make the determination of a state-sponsored genocide like the one targeting the Rohingya.

item.title: NPR: GOP Sen. Johnson rejects tying government funding to an end to the Iran war
item.description: "We're not going to shut down the war," Sen. Ron Johnson said as Republicans and Democrats struggle to reach a government funding deal.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Iran war has permanently reshaped energy priorities, IEA report says
item.description: The repercussions from the Iran war will "leave lasting marks" on the world's energy sector, said the Paris-based IEA, founded after the 1973-74 oil crisis.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: U.S. Capitol Christmas tree arrives in D.C.
item.description: Placing a tree outside the Capitol building has been a tradition for more than 60 years.

item.title: NPR: Trump to hold press conference after meeting with Xi and Putin
item.description: Trump did not formally take questions while in China at the end of his trip, though it's typically expected on presidential foreign trips.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump administration moves to have lawsuit dismissed in challenge to Alaska's U.S. Senate race
item.description: In their filing, Justice Department attorneys urged the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals to overturn the lower court's dismissal of the case to erase the loss, but then dismiss the case anyway.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: White House taps Kirsten Davies as cyber chief after outages rattle Americans
item.description: The White House named a new national cyber director Thursday after a series of widespread service outages disrupted life and unnerved many Americans.

item.title: NPR: Texas execution took over an hour as staff struggled to find vein; Reinaldo Dennes moaned about pain
item.description: The same day Dennes was given lethal injection, Florida carried out a record-breaking 20th execution of the year.

item.title: NPR: Dems aim to block Iran war funding. And, Army delays lead azide detonation in Iowa
item.description: Congress needs to pass a funding measure to avoid a shutdown next month, providing Dems an opportunity to leverage power. And, the Army says waiting to detonate lead azide could become dangerous.

item.title: NPR: Senate passes bipartisan energy bill amid environmental concerns
item.description: As Americans struggle with rising energy costs and increased demand driven by AI, the Senate passed a bipartisan bill that will speed up the approval process for data centers and power plants.

item.title: NPR: New York City unveils a bold plan to move its jails off Rikers Island
item.description: New York City officials are moving forward with plans to close Rikers, the city's main jail complex, after years of discussion. The jail has been plagued by assaults and inmate deaths.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Do you need a measles booster shot now that the U.S. has lost its elimination status?
item.description: The U.S., Mexico and Bolivia lost their measles-free status this week after stubborn outbreaks erased decades of progress.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: FCC votes to allow state prisons to jam signals from contraband cellphones
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission on Thursday acted to allow state prisons across the United States to jam the signals of cellphones smuggled to inmates as the federal government cracks down on devices that authorities say are the No. 1 security threat in the nation's correctional facilities.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Inside the historic summit between Trump, Xi and Putin
item.description: It was the summit seen around the world. The first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia resulted in a joint statement that included promises to release more oil and hold formal talks about nuclear weapons. Nick Schifrin reports from Shenzhen.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Experts assess what was addressed and overlooked at trilateral meeting in China
item.description: For perspective on the Trump, Xi and Putin summit in China, Amna Nawaz spoke with Dennis Wilder and Fred Fleitz. Wilder was senior director for East Asia and special assistant to President George W. Bush and was the editor of the president's daily brief during the Obama administration. Fleitz was the National Security Council chief of staff during the first Trump administration.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Russian drone attack damages Dutch embassy and cathedral in Ukraine
item.description: In our news wrap Thursday, a Russian drone damaged the Dutch embassy and a cathedral in Ukraine, President Trump says he posthumously pardoned Pete Rose, record-breaking rains inundated parts of Florida's Atlantic coast and the Cincinnati Zoo says its famous hippo, Fiona, died after she swallowed a visitor's hat.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Anthropic's trillion-dollar valuation tests its promise to develop AI responsibly
item.description: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic completed the largest initial public offering of all time. Even as CEO Dario Amodei celebrated the huge launch, he reiterated his commitment to developing artificial intelligence responsibly. William Brangham discussed more with Jessica Lessin, the editor-in-chief of the technology website The Information.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: International Court of Justice finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
item.description: A historic judgment from the International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority. The ruling comes years after Myanmar's Muslim minority was forced to flee. Stephanie Sy discusses what the genocide verdict means for international law and the future of the Rohingya people with Adil Ahmad Haque, author of "Law and Morality at War."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Americans will pay more for Thanksgiving dinners this year, says Farm Bureau survey
item.description: High diesel prices have made it more expensive for farmers to process and transport Thanksgiving staples like milk, dinner rolls, potatoes and cranberries, the Farm Bureau said.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Tennessee Democrat describes how she won a Trump district with almost no ad money
item.description: When Democrats take control of the House, one of their new members will hail from a district no one expected them to win. Victoria Broderick is a tech support worker from rural Tennessee who unseated eight-term Republican Rep. Scott Desjarlais. She did so despite raising less than $100,000 and receiving zero investment from the national party. Liz Landers spoke with Broderick about her win.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'Huna' wins National Book Award, but author denied visa to attend ceremony
item.description: At the National Book Awards, Abdelrahman ElGendy won the nonfiction prize for his book "Huna," a memoir of his six years as a political prisoner in Egypt. But ElGendy wasn't there to accept the award. His visa to travel from Europe was denied by the U.S. government. Amna Nawaz spoke with ElGendy for our arts and culture series, CANVAS.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: House music pioneer Crystal Waters celebrates the genre's influence and impact
item.description: In New York, house music pioneer Crystal Waters is bringing together major figures like Deborah Cox and Billy Porter with a live orchestra. It's all to celebrate the genre's 30-year legacy. Geoff Bennett spoke with Waters about "I Am House Orchestrated" and how the music has grown into both a cultural revolution and a space for self-expression. It's for our arts and culture series, CANVAS.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 3 takeaways from Trump, Xi and Putin's historic summit
item.description: The meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin on Thursday was the first-ever sit-down for the leaders of the three countries.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Prosecutor declines to charge Wisconsin officer who fatally shot Black man in Madison
item.description: The Wisconsin police officer who shot and killed a 38-year-old Black man in Madison in July will not face criminal charges, a prosecutor announced Thursday, sparking calls for justice from the victim's family members and community advocates.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Judge issues 14-day extension of order blocking Trump's triumphal arch construction
item.description: A federal judge on Wednesday temporarily extended an order blocking the Trump administration from breaking ground on a towering memorial arch in the nation's capital.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Ella Langley sweeps the 2026 CMA Awards and wins entertainer of the year
item.description: It didn't take a crystal ball to see: The 2026 Country Music Association Awards were always going to be all about Ella Langley.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Cincinnati Zoo says Fiona the hippo has died, more than a week after ingesting a hat
item.description: "It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency," the zoo said in a statement.

item.title: NPR: Top House Democrat questions what Trump accomplished in Xi-Putin summit
item.description: Rep. Gregory Meeks raises concerns about U.S. alliances after Trump's summit with Xi and Putin. He also discusses Chinese espionage amid the Nvidia scandal.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Fact-checking Mullin's House hearing on FAA ground stop, outages and dirty bombs
item.description: Following a week of flight delays, website outages and the possibility of an Iranian dirty bomb attack, House lawmakers grilled top administration officials, including Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, about threats to the United States.

item.title: NPR: Judges have put Trump's arch and golf course on hold, but only for a matter of days
item.description: A federal judge has twice delayed construction of Trump's arch. Another is keeping East Potomac Park open. The proposed golf course redesign got mixed feedback from a federal arts panel on Thursday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Iowans brace for lead dust cloud as Army plans to detonate 5 tons of bomb-making chemicals
item.description: Plans by the U.S. Army to detonate about 5 tons of bomb-making chemicals that have become unusable and might explode if moved have residents in southeast Iowa worried that a cloud of lead dust could cause environmental contamination and health problems.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mississippi saw a spike in 'inactive' voters for the midterms. Democratic lawmakers want answers
item.description: Lawmakers want an investigation and legislation to ensure that eligible voters are not mistakenly moved to inactive status, especially as the party tries to maintain its political momentum going into next year's race for governor.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: NASA's Voyager 1 calls Earth from more than 16 billion miles, or one light-day, away
item.description: It marked another day in the history books for Voyager 1, which launched in 1977.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Kushner says Russia is 'comfortable' with NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine to end war after Trump talks with Putin
item.description: Ukrainian officials fear their country's fate could be determined by agreements between Trump and Putin, raising concerns among European governments.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Are tech disruptions and and outages the new normal?
item.description: The Trump administration maintains there is "zero" indication that the latest outages are linked, or caused by bad actors like cybercriminals.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'I'm not MAGA,' Elon Musk says after Republicans' midterm thrashing
item.description: Musk told The New York Times' DealBook Summit audience Wednesday he feels foolish for spending so much on the midterms.

item.title: NPR: 'Bigger than Barack Obama's election': Scholars reflect on Mississippi Senate race
item.description: Scott Colom is now this Southern state's first Black U.S. senator in nearly 150 years. Scholars and Mississippi natives Eddie Glaude and Kiese Laymon discuss the historic significance of his victory.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: For Putin, sharing a spotlight with Trump and Xi boosts his profile on the global stage
item.description: For Russian President Vladimir Putin, Thursday's three-way meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping offered a much-coveted chance for the Kremlin leader to demonstrate that he heads a superpower on a par with the United States and China.

item.title: NPR: The U.N.'s top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar security forces "acted with genocidal intent" against the Rohingya during military operations in the northern Rakhine state in 2017.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Republican Rep. Nick Begich wins reelection for Alaska House seat
item.description: His win Wednesday through the state's ranked vote tabulation process was a rare bright spot for Republicans, whose ranks in the House were decimated in the midterms.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: UN's highest court finds Myanmar responsible for genocide in historic ruling
item.description: In a landmark judgment, the United Nations' top court ruled Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in a brutal 2017 military operation and ordered the Southeast Asian nation to allow people who fled the violence to return home.

item.title: NPR: The midterms were the largest win for either party in 50 years
item.description: Some 56% of people cast votes for Democrats in House races, compared to 42% who voted Republican. That 14-point spread is the widest win for either party in 50 years, since after Watergate.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: No breakthroughs from Trump, Xi and Putin's 3-way talks on nuclear risks
item.description: They were to discuss the wars in Ukraine and Iran and how to reduce the dangers posed by nuclear arsenals. But after roughly 70 minutes behind closed doors, they agreed to a far narrower agenda.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Fiona the hippo swallowed a hat. The Cincinnati Zoo hopes a little shake will help get it out
item.description: Surgery isn't an option for full-grown hippos.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Senate meets for legislative business as Trump returns from Putin-Xi talks in China
item.description: Democratic Sen. Tim Kaine says he will force a vote on the Senate floor in the coming weeks to require President Donald Trump's administration to calculate the human rights consequences of its policies in Russia.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Anthropic set to begin trading as a $1.5 trillion company in the biggest IPO on record
item.description: Anthropic decided to barrel ahead with the IPO despite jitters among some investors over market volatility, a potential regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led Congress next year and growing anti-AI sentiment among the public.

item.title: NPR: Incoming House majority leader Katherine Clark stresses Democratic unity
item.description: As Democrats prepare to take control of the House, incoming majority leader Katherine Clark discusses the party's ambitious agenda and divisions within its ranks.

item.title: NPR: Democrats formally nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker of the House
item.description: The New York Democrat moved a step closer to becoming the first Black lawmaker in U.S. history to serve in the job, after House Democrats voted overwhelmingly to support him.

item.title: NPR: Top U.N. court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar security forces "acted with genocidal intent" against the Rohingya during the 2017 military operations in the northern Rakhine State.

item.title: NPR: Anthropic raises more than $100B in IPO. And, Dems nominate Jeffries for House speaker
item.description: Despite growing concern over a possible AI bubble, Anthropic had a record-breaking initial public offering. And, Hakeem Jeffries could become the first Black Speaker of the House.

item.title: NPR: Trump, Xi and Putin meet as global alliances hang in the balance
item.description: President Trump, Xi and Putin have met in Shenzhen for a historic trilateral meeting, with Ukraine, Iran and nuclear disarmament on the agenda.

item.title: NPR: Ben Shapiro on conservative media and the future of the Republican Party
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep sits down with conservative commentator Ben Shapiro to discuss the future of the Republican party.

item.title: NPR: House Democrat warns 13 Trump allies to save their records for upcoming investigations
item.description: Among the recipients of letters from Robert Garcia, incoming chair of the House Oversight Committee, are Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, Jared Kushner and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller.

item.title: NPR: Mary Peltola flips Alaska's Senate seat. And, Nvidia won't reinstate Jensen Huang
item.description: Former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola has won one of the U.S.' most watched Senate races. And, Nvidia's board says it doesn't plan to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang despite pressure from his allies.

item.title: NPR: Ben Shapiro on the future of the Republican Party and conservative media
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep sits down with conservative commentator Ben Shapiro to discuss the future of the Republican party.

item.title: NPR: International Court of Justice to issue ruling on Myanmar genocide case
item.description: The International Court of Justice delivers a landmark ruling on Thursday whether Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya — a historic test of international justice that could reshape state accountability for genocide worldwide.

item.title: NPR: Markwayne Mullin testifies before Congress after series of nationwide tech outages
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin testified before Congress about global security threats facing the nation. The recent cyber and technology problems dominated the annual hearing.

item.title: NPR: Democratic Black women take over almost all state agencies in Georgia soon
item.description: In January, most of Georgia's state agencies will be headed by Black women who were all elected in the 2026 midterms.

item.title: NPR: The law releasing the Epstein files passed one year ago. What do his victims say?
item.description: It's been a year since the House passed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, forcing the Justice Department to release millions of files connected to the convicted sex offender. His victims speak out.

item.title: NPR: Why the Nvidia scandal is a national security issue
item.description: The Nvidia scandal has spilled over into the Trump administration, which is now under intense scrutiny for how it allowed America's top AI chips to end up in China's hands.

item.title: NPR: Democrats nominate Jeffries for speaker, prep investigations into Trump's orbit
item.description: Democrats gave the official nod to Hakeem Jeffries to be the next speaker of the House. Meanwhile, Democrats are ramping up their plans to investigate the Trump administration come January.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 per share, valuing the AI giant at $1.5 trillion
item.description: The higher-than-anticipated pricing signals broad investor enthusiasm for AI stocks even amid some uncertainty in the market stemming from the ouster of Nvidia's CEO and worries about an AI bubble.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Rainfall supercharged by El Niño causes road flooding, synagogue roof collapse in South Florida
item.description: A slow-moving storm system dumped heavy rains that prompted an emergency declaration Wednesday in South Florida where the roof of a synagogue collapsed and cars were submerged along roads, authorities said.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Iran widens Gulf attacks by targeting U.S. air base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain
item.description: Iran said that its recent attacks — including those on other U.S. facilities in Bahrain on Sunday and Friday — were in response to U.S. drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Why Grand Theft Auto VI's release is a major cultural moment
item.description: One of the biggest entertainment launches in history is underway with billions of dollars at stake. It's the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, the latest edition of the long-awaited and controversial video game. If you're wondering what all the hype is about, Tim McPhillips has a helpful guide.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: On 'Settle In,' Min Jin Lee and Amna Nawaz discuss the real stories behind her novels
item.description: Best-selling author Min Jin Lee spends years meticulously researching her novels. Her latest, "American Hagwon," examines the pressures and aspirations surrounding education in Korean culture. She joined Amna Nawaz to discuss the extensive interviewing behind her work and how she captures the immigrant experience.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump lands in China for trade talks and high-stakes summit with Xi and Putin
item.description: President Trump landed in southern China after signing a trade deal and pledging increased defense cooperation with the Philippines. On Thursday, Trump will hold a historic summit with the Chinese and Russian presidents on the sidelines of a meeting of Asia-Pacific countries in Shenzhen, China. Nick Schifrin reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Former national security staffer on how presidents prepare for talks with world leaders
item.description: For perspective on President Trump's trip to China and how foreign governments assess the president, Amna Nawaz spoke with Julia Curlee. She's a former CIA analyst and served on the National Security Council staff during the Biden and Trump administrations. She's now a public service fellow at Lawfare, a publication that focuses on national security.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker of the House
item.description: In our news wrap Wednesday, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries moved a step closer today to becoming the next Speaker of the House, Democrats have secured a 56-to-44 majority in the Senate after Mary Peltola won the last outstanding race in Alaska and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new military agreement with Venezuela.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Lawmakers press Mullin on flight disruptions and ICE tactics
item.description: National security officials from the Trump administration were on Capitol Hill on Wednesday, and lawmakers had plenty of questions about the series of outages and cyber problems that have alarmed millions. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton sought to reassure Americans during their testimony. Stephanie Sy reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Republicans need to focus on 'quality of life issues,' ousted GOP Rep. Lawler says
item.description: More than 30 House Republican incumbents lost their seats in the general election amid this year's blue wave. One of those is Rep. Mike Lawler of New York. Lawler earned a reputation as a moderate, willing to buck his own party, and was rated one of the most bipartisan members of Congress during his time in office. Amna Nawaz spoke with Lawler about the midterm results and the future of the GOP.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Paris Hilton pushes for law against deepfakes: 'I want to help build a world that's safe'
item.description: The growing use of artificial intelligence to create sexually explicit images of people without their consent is raising new concerns about privacy, exploitation and the laws meant to protect victims. Among those calling for greater protections is Paris Hilton. She was on Capitol Hill this week urging lawmakers to pass the bipartisan DEFIANCE Act. Liz Landers reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What we've learned from Voyager 1 as it reaches extraordinary milestone
item.description: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft has reached an extraordinary milestone — traveling so far from Earth that it now takes a full day for light, or a radio signal, to reach it. Launched nearly 50 years ago, Voyager 1 is the farthest any human-made object has ever traveled, and the first spacecraft to enter interstellar space. Miles O'Brien puts this achievement in perspective and explains what comes next.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: High school valedictorians to get custom kicks after Sen.-elect Colom asks Nike to 'Just Do It'
item.description: Nike is gifting high school valedictorians across the country with a pair of custom sneakers after Mississippi's incoming senator appealed to the company on social media.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: AP report: Bernie Sanders unveils how he'll push for Medicare for All when Democrats take power
item.description: Sen. Bernie Sanders is preparing to use his return atop a powerful Senate committee to push for sweeping changes to the nation's healthcare system, setting up an early test of how far Democrats are willing to go in embracing progressive priorities.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats flipped 9 US Senate seats — the most in almost 70 years
item.description: Former Rep. Mary Peltola's victory over Republican incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska's competitive U.S. Senate race has flipped a ninth Republican-held seat to the Democrats, giving Peltola's party its biggest midterm gain in nearly 70 years.

item.title: NPR: Democratic strategists think Montana House race could hold the secret to future wins
item.description: Montana is sending a Democrat to the U.S. House for the first time in three decades. Many in the party think Sam Forstag's campaign may be a playbook for how Democrats can win again in rural America.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Will people skip work and hurt the U.S. economy to play Grand Theft Auto 6?
item.description: Are you a gamer who's planning to suddenly be struck by a stomach bug on Nov. 19? Or did you request paid time off that day?

item.title: PBS NewsHour: From pop stars to poets to politicians, hundreds gathering for joyful tribute to Gloria Steinem
item.description: Luminaries from political figures to pop stars to poets were gathering Wednesday in Manhattan for a joyful and music-filled tribute to Gloria Steinem, the trailblazing activist, prolific author and most visible symbol of American feminism.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Cornyn blocks top Justice Department official nominated for judicial vacancy in Texas
item.description: A senior outgoing Republican senator said Wednesday that he will block one of President Donald Trump's final judicial picks for a court vacancy in Texas, as the GOP-led Senate scrambles to fill all the remaining vacancies in the federal courts before Democrats assume power in January.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: DOT Secretary Sean Duffy keeps blaming L3Harris after FAA ground stop, even as cause remains unknown
item.description: U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy continues to blame a contractor for the events that prompted the Federal Aviation Administration to order a ground stop last week, even though investigators haven't determined the root cause.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Muslims are projected to outnumber Christians by 2035 as the world's largest religion
item.description: Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035, according to detailed projections released Wednesday by the Pew Research Center.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Voyager 1 is now a light-day from Earth. Here's what to know about NASA's longest-running mission
item.description: It's the little space probe that could: Nearly 50 years after it was launched, NASA's Voyager 1 on Wednesday became the first human-made object to travel one light-day — or 16 billion miles — away from Earth.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Intelligence official pressed to explain cause of National Security Agency outage
item.description: Jay Clayton, the Trump administration's director of national intelligence, said Wednesday that recent computer systems service disruptions in the government and private sector are "not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack."

item.title: NPR: As overdose deaths fall, White House makes misleading claims about who deserves credit
item.description: In a statement celebrating the historic drop in drug deaths, the White House pointed to successes since President Trump took office. In fact, the biggest progress happened under the Biden administration.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Hegseth meets with Venezuelan interim leaders in latest Trump Cabinet visit since Maduro's ouster
item.description: Secretary Pete Hegseth's visit comes at a time of uncertainty for Venezuelans regarding who will lead the nation in the coming months and years.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' arrives with enormous hype and expectations after 13-year wait
item.description: After a 13-year wait, one of entertainment's biggest releases is finally here.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump plans to meet separately with Putin on his China trip in addition to their 3-way talks with Xi
item.description: President Donald Trump plans to meet separately with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday in China, in addition to their already scheduled three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, a U.S. official confirmed.

item.title: NPR: Veteran reporter asks SCOTUS to hear case on protecting confidential sources
item.description: A longtime national security reporter is facing steep fines in a civil lawsuit for failing to disclose her source. She's asking the Supreme Court to weigh in.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to become House speaker, a historic first
item.description: Jeffries brushed past skeptics and was on track to make history as the nation's first Black American with the gavel.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: DHS Secretary Mullin testifies on worldwide threats amid tech outages, Iran warnings
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is set to appear Wednesday at a congressional hearing about threats facing the country at a time of looming questions over cyber infrastructure, the future of immigration enforcement and his decision to fly to the LSU-Texas college football game as travelers across the U.S. were still stuck at airports after the nationwide grounding of flights.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate seat, beating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan
item.description: The Alaska race was the last U.S. Senate contest to be resolved in this year's midterm elections and gave Democrats a 56-44 majority after they flipped nine GOP-held seats to retake the chamber.

item.title: NPR: How the East Potomac golf course became a D.C. landmark — and what could happen to it
item.description: A federal judge is keeping East Potomac Park open for now, but hasn't ordered the government to keep the municipal golf course operational.

item.title: NPR: Trump lands in China with key meetings with Xi and Putin on the agenda
item.description: Xi paid Trump a special honor by greeting him on the tarmac after Air Force One arrived in Shenzhen, reciprocating a gesture made by the U.S. president during Xi's visit to Washington in September.

item.title: NPR: How the East Potomac golf course became a D.C. landmark — and what could happen to it
item.description: A federal judge is keeping East Potomac Park open for now, but hasn't ordered the government to keep the municipal golf course operational.
